title: The Lead Belt
dek: 44 contaminated sites each have a school within 500 metres — placing an estimated 58,000 students near extreme soil lead levels with zero permanent closures on public record.
summary: 44 contaminated sites sit within 500 metres of a school each, exposing an estimated 58,000 students to extreme soil lead levels. Zero sites have been permanently closed.
key_findings: 44 contaminated sites identified each have at least one school within a 500-metre radius, placing an estimated 58,000 students in close proximity to sites with extreme soil lead levels.
Zero permanent site closures appear on public record despite documented contamination levels consistent with the icddr,b and Stanford 2025 study findings.
Three sites have been independently verified as active through satellite imagery analysis, confirming ongoing contamination risk at the time of publication.
rtl_status: RTI requests filed with DoE and DIFE — responses pending

title: The Impunity Machine
dek: A data-driven investigation into the institutional mechanisms that allow environmental and labour violations to persist without consequence.
summary: A forensic examination of the institutional mechanisms that allow documented environmental and labour violations to persist without prosecution or penalty.
key_findings: Institutional inspections of environmental violations occurred on average 14 months after the initial public report, permitting ongoing contamination.
Less than 3% of documented labour safety violations resulted in financial penalties, with zero criminal prosecutions on record.
Over 70% of factories violating local pollution limits retained their green category status due to self-reporting exemptions.
